To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the only factor affecting the collection efficiency of autologous peripheral blood hematopoietic stem cells was preprocedure absolute peripheral CD34+ cells and that collection efficiency was higher when the ComTec was used with a 4 L bag.
preprocedure absolute CD 34+ cells is the only independent factor that affects the collection efficiency of peripheral blood stem cells.
preprocedure absolute CD-34+ cells count is the only independent factor that affects the CE and the CE2 is more accurate indicator of the CE than the CE1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the collection efficiency of peripheral blood progenitor cells (CD34+ cells).
the factors affecting CE and the accuracy of CE1 and CE 2.
the factors affecting collection efficiency and the formula to calculate the collection efficiency of the autologous peripheral blood progenitor cell harvests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the preprocedure absolute CD 34 count is an important factor in determining the CE, and the CE2 is more accurate than CE1.
CE is not affected by any patient or procedural factor except preprocedure CD34+ cells count.
preprocedure absolute CD4+ count was the only independent variable affecting CE and the mean CE2 (49.1) was slightly higher than CE1 (41.2) but was not statistically significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CE1 and CE are both acceptable indicators for quality assessment of leukaphereses.
apheresis procedure with high preprocedure CD34+ cell counts and high preprocedure absolute CD4+ cells will yield more CD34+ cells.
a higher preprocedure absolute CD 34+ count is an important factor for a successful apheresis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preprocedure absolute CD4+ cells are the most significant predictor of CE.
the CE2 formula should be used as a better indicator of CE, which takes into account the impact of mobilization of stem cell during the apheresis procedure.
the quality of apheresis program can be assessed objectively by calculating CE, which can help in identifying and rectifying any deficiencies in the program.
